title: Gilroy 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: Gilroy 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: Gilroy 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for Gilroy cold storage and ag-processing buildings, the Premium Outlets retail draw, and Highway 101 distribution space.

sections.html: Gilroy still runs on agriculture as much as anything else, and its commercial real estate reflects that even as distribution and retail have grown up around it. Cold storage and processing buildings tied to the surrounding farmland sit alongside the Premium Outlets retail draw and a growing stock of distribution space that takes advantage of land prices well below the rest of Santa Clara County. An exchanger identifying Gilroy replacement property should expect a wider spread of building types and price points here than in the more built-out cities to the north. The city's position at the southern end of Santa Clara County, where Highway 101 and Highway 152 meet, also makes it a natural staging point for goods moving toward the Central Valley, which supports distribution demand beyond what Gilroy's own population would otherwise generate.

sections.heading: Cold Storage and Agricultural Processing Buildings
sections.html: Gilroy's agricultural processing and cold storage buildings serve growers and packers across South Santa Clara County, and these buildings carry specialized infrastructure, refrigeration systems, loading configurations, and sometimes onsite wastewater treatment, that ordinary industrial buyers do not need to evaluate elsewhere. A replacement property buyer should confirm the condition and remaining service life of refrigeration equipment specifically, since replacing a cold storage system is a significant capital expense that can change the economics of the deal if it is closer to end of life than the listing suggests. Insulation quality and floor drainage also matter more here than in a typical dry warehouse, and a buyer should walk the building during an active shift where possible to see how the current tenant's actual workflow uses the space.

sections.heading: The Premium Outlets and Highway 101 Retail Draw
sections.html: The outlet center just off Highway 101 pulls shoppers from well beyond Gilroy itself, and retail parcels near that interchange benefit from traffic counts closer to a regional draw than a typical small-town retail corridor would generate. A buyer identifying retail replacement property near this interchange should review actual traffic and visibility data for the specific parcel, since proximity to the outlet center does not automatically mean every nearby parcel captures the same drive-by exposure.

sections.heading: Distribution and Logistics Space on Cheaper South County Land
sections.html:
Land costs in Gilroy run meaningfully below San Jose and the Peninsula, which has drawn distribution and logistics tenants who need larger footprints than they could afford closer to the urban core while still reaching Highway 101 quickly. A diligence file for a Gilroy distribution property typically includes:

  • Refrigeration system age and remaining service life for cold storage buildings
  • Traffic count and visibility data for retail parcels near the outlet interchange
  • Clear height and truck court depth for distribution buildings
  • Water and wastewater capacity documentation, particularly for agricultural processing uses
  • Confirmation of seasonal versus year-round tenant occupancy patterns
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

A buyer should confirm whether a given tenant's operation is seasonal, common among agricultural processors, before underwriting a stabilized twelve-month income stream. Water rights and well capacity are worth confirming separately from municipal utility service for any parcel that draws on agricultural wells rather than the city system, since well output can vary from one property to the next even within the same immediate area.

sections.heading: Identification Timing for Seasonal Agricultural Tenants
sections.html: Because some Gilroy agricultural processing tenants scale operations up and down with the growing season, an exchanger identifying this type of replacement property should review at least a full year of trailing income and expense data before the 45-day deadline, rather than a snapshot from the property's busiest months. Naming a seasonal agricultural building alongside a steadier retail or distribution candidate under the 200% rule gives the exchanger a way to compare income stability across very different asset types before making a final decision.

sections.heading: Qualified Intermediary Coordination for Land-Heavy Parcels
sections.html: Gilroy transactions often involve more land relative to building square footage than deals closer to San Jose, and a qualified intermediary should confirm early whether the land itself, separate from any structure, qualifies for like-kind treatment alongside the building. This content describes process and coordination only; an exchanger should confirm the specific like-kind analysis for a land-heavy Gilroy parcel with a tax advisor before signing the exchange agreement.

faqs.q: What makes Gilroy cold storage buildings different to underwrite?
faqs.a: These buildings carry specialized refrigeration and sometimes onsite wastewater treatment, and a buyer should confirm the remaining service life of that equipment specifically, since replacement is a significant capital expense that changes the deal's economics.

faqs.q: Does every parcel near the Gilroy outlet interchange get the same retail traffic?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. A buyer should review actual traffic and visibility data for the specific parcel rather than assuming proximity to the outlet center alone guarantees the same drive-by exposure as the anchor retail itself.

faqs.q: Why has distribution demand grown in Gilroy specifically?
faqs.a: Land costs here run well below San Jose and the Peninsula, which lets logistics tenants take larger footprints than they could afford closer to the urban core while still reaching Highway 101 quickly.

faqs.q: How should I underwrite a seasonal agricultural processing tenant?
faqs.a: Review at least a full year of trailing income and expense data rather than a snapshot from the busiest growing-season months, since seasonal swings can make a short window of data misleading.

faqs.q: Does the land itself matter separately from the building in a Gilroy exchange?
faqs.a: Often yes, since Gilroy deals frequently involve more land relative to building square footage than deals closer to San Jose, and a qualified intermediary should confirm early how the land component fits the like-kind analysis.
